To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the organizational context factors moderate and shape the installed integration and the separation mechanisms between the two business models, the integration and separation between the business models occur in all elements of the business model, and the separation mechanisms are more important for the online business model than for the traditional business model.
the organizational context factors moderate integration and separation mechanisms that are used to balance tensions between traditional and online magazine publishing business models.

“the organizational context and the business model elements moderate the installed integration and the separation mechanisms between the dual business models, which are the result of a trade-off process”.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding the interplay between the two business models and how this interplay can be managed.
the organizational context factors that influence the interplay between the traditional and online business model and the installed integration mechanisms between these two models.
the organizational context and integration mechanisms between two conflicting business models, the traditional and online ones, within the same organization.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

, in the context of a traditional and online business model coexistence, integration mechanisms occur along all business model elements and separation mechanisms along all business model components as well.

the integration and separation between two conflicting business models are a continuous and dynamic process, where separation and integration mechanisms are constantly changing and evolving, and the organizational context is an important moderator.
the integration and separation between two conflicting business models is a complex task that is not only related to the business model elements but also to the organizational context.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a company can successfully manage two conflicting business models by using the organizational context factors to guide the integration and separation of the two business models.
the integration and separation between the two business models is not only spatial, as it is commonly assumed, but also occurs along the other business model elements.
the integration and separation of business models is not only a question of spatial separation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the integration of the business models is a dynamic, continuous, and complex process that is not only driven by the organizational context factors, but also by the elements of a business models.
the separation of the business models is a necessary but insufficient condition to achieve organizational ambidexterity.
the organizational context factors are the main moderators of the mechanisms used to manage two conflicting business models.
